questions.explanation: Formula: CV = (s/x̄) × 100. Steps: From Q2, s ≈ 7.55, x̄ = 13. CV = 7.55/13 = 0.581 ≈ 0.58. Result: Between 0.5 and 1.0.

questions.explanation: Formula: Median = middle value when sorted. Steps: Sort: 5, 6, 6, 12, 20, 20, 22. For n=7 (odd), median = 4th value = 12. Result: 12.

questions.question_text: The number of deliveries done in a day by 7 different sales executives working for an e-commerce retailer is recorded to be 12, 22, 20, 6, 5, 6, and 20. The inter-quartile range for the number of deliveries done by a sales executive in a day is:
questions.explanation: Formula: IQR = Q3 - Q1. Steps: Sorted: 5, 6, 6, 12, 20, 20, 22. Q1 position = 0.25(7+1) = 2, Q1 = 6. Q3 position = 0.75(7+1) = 6, Q3 = 20. IQR = 20 - 6 = 14. Result: 14.

questions.question_text: The number of deliveries done in a day by 7 different sales executives working for an e-commerce retailer is recorded to be 12, 22, 20, 6, 5, 6, and 20. The z-score corresponding to the median number of deliveries done by a sales executive in a day is:
questions.explanation: Formula: z = (x - x̄)/s. Steps: Median = 12, x̄ = 13, s ≈ 7.55. z = (12 - 13)/7.55 = -1/7.55 ≈ -0.13. Result: Between -1 and 0.

questions.explanation: Formula: Mean = Σx/n. Steps: Sum = 12+22+20+6+5+6+20 = 91. n = 7. Mean = 91/7 = 13. Result: Between 12 and 14.

questions.question_text: The number of deliveries done in a day by 7 different sales executives working for an e-commerce retailer is recorded to be 12, 22, 20, 6, 5, 6, and 20. The number of outliers in this data identified using the box-plot method is:
questions.explanation: Formula: Outliers if value < Q1 - 1.5×IQR or > Q3 + 1.5×IQR. Steps: Q1 = 6, Q3 = 20, IQR = 14. Lower fence = 6 - 1.5×14 = -15. Upper fence = 20 + 1.5×14 = 41. All values (5 to 22) are within [-15, 41]. Result: 0 outliers.

questions.question_text: The number of deliveries done in a day by 7 different sales executives working for an e-commerce retailer is recorded to be 12, 22, 20, 6, 5, 6, and 20. The 40th percentile corresponding to the number of deliveries done by a sales executive in a day is:
questions.explanation: Formula: Percentile position = (n+1)×p/100. Steps: n = 7, p = 40. Position = 0.40(7+1) = 3.2. Sorted: 5, 6, 6, 12, 20, 20, 22. Interpolate: 6 + 0.2×(12-6) = 6 + 1.2 = 7.2. Result: Between 7 and 8.

questions.question_text: A random sample of 60 boys and 60 girls that registered for placement at a college was analyzed to see how many received 1, 2 or 3 interviews. The survey showed that 10 boys received only one job interview, while 75% of the girls received 3 job interviews. Further, only 25% of the boys received 2 interviews, but the number of boys receiving 2 interviews exceeded the number of girls receiving 2 interviews by 5. The probability that a randomly selected student from this survey is a girl that received only 1 interview is:
questions.explanation: Steps: Boys with 1 interview = 10. Girls with 3 interviews = 75% of 60 = 45. Boys with 2 interviews = 25% of 60 = 15. Girls with 2 interviews = 15 - 5 = 10. Girls with 1 interview = 60 - 45 - 10 = 5. Total students = 120. P(Girl ∩ 1 interview) = 5/120 = 0.042. Result: Between 0 and 0.25.

questions.question_text: A random sample of 60 boys and 60 girls that registered for placement at a college was analyzed to see how many received 1, 2 or 3 interviews. The survey showed that 10 boys received only one job interview, while 75% of the girls received 3 job interviews. Further, only 25% of the boys received 2 interviews, but the number of boys receiving 2 interviews exceeded the number of girls receiving 2 interviews by 5. The probability that a randomly selected student from this survey is either a boy or a student that received exactly 2 interviews is:
questions.explanation: Formula: P(Boy ∪ 2 interviews) = P(Boy) + P(2 interviews) - P(Boy ∩ 2 interviews). Steps: P(Boy) = 60/120 = 0.5. P(2 interviews) = (15+10)/120 = 25/120 = 0.208. P(Boy ∩ 2) = 15/120 = 0.125. P(Boy ∪ 2) = 0.5 + 0.208 - 0.125 = 0.583. Result: Between 0.50 and 0.75.
